name: Microsoft 365
summary: Microsoft does not review your app, but other organisations' admins usually must consent to mail and calendar access, and multi-tenant apps should be publisher verified.

capabilities.label: Read email
capabilities.alternative: No user-consentable way to read mail in tenants on Microsoft's default policy.

capabilities.label: Manage calendar
capabilities.alternative: Admin consent in tenants on Microsoft's default policy.

capabilities.label: Read contacts
capabilities.alternative: Contacts.ReadWrite needs admin consent since mid-2026.

paths.label: Own single-tenant app for your workspace
paths.drivenBy: Needs an Azure account with an active subscription and at least the Application Developer role in your tenant. Name field and account type set at registration.
paths.costNote: An active Azure subscription is required; no fee for registration is stated.
paths.next: In the Entra admin center go to Entra ID > App registrations > New registration and add the Composio redirect URI.

paths.label: Other organisations, user-consentable scopes
paths.drivenBy: Users in many tenants can't consent to unverified multi-tenant apps, so get publisher verified; send-mail and read-contacts scopes stay user-consentable.
paths.waitOfficial: 3–5 business days to vet your partner account; verification then takes minutes
paths.waitReported: Weeks to months when partner vetting is rejected
paths.costNote: Microsoft charges no fee for publisher verification.
paths.next: Start AI Cloud Partner Program verification today; it gates publisher verification.

untilApproved.text: Unverified multi-tenant apps show 'Unverified', and users in tenants with step-up consent cannot consent (AADSTS90094).

paths.label: Other organisations, mail or calendar access
paths.drivenBy: In tenants on Microsoft's default consent policy, users can't consent to mail or calendar scopes: each customer's admin must, even for a verified app.
paths.waitOfficial: 3–5 business days to vet your partner account; verification then takes minutes
paths.waitReported: Weeks to months when partner vetting is rejected
paths.costNote: Microsoft charges no fee for publisher verification.
paths.next: Start partner verification today and build an admin-consent step into every customer's onboarding.

untilApproved.text: Each customer's admin must grant consent to mail and calendar scopes, verified or not.
Unverified multi-tenant apps show 'Unverified', and step-up consent blocks users entirely.

prereqs.text: A verified AI Cloud Partner Program account
prereqs.why: Needed for publisher verification. Vetting checks government ID, domain and business registration; usually 3–5 business days.

prereqs.text: A work or school Entra tenant
prereqs.why: Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account can never be publisher verified.

prereqs.text: A custom domain verified in that tenant
prereqs.why: *.onmicrosoft.com is not accepted as a publisher domain.

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: Sign in with az login (you), then the agent registers it. Choose 'Multiple Entra ID tenants' to serve other organisations. The app object can't move between tenants later.

values.label: Azure CLI
values.text: az ad app create --display-name "Your agent" --sign-in-audience AzureADMultipleOrgs --web-redirect-uris https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URI to the app registration
steps.detail: Paste the redirect URI from your Composio auth config. HTTPS only (http just for localhost), case-sensitive, at most 256 characters; a mismatch fails with AADSTS50011.

steps.title: Create a client secret and add the Microsoft Graph permissions you need
steps.detail: Certificates & secrets → New client secret (24 months at most; Microsoft recommends under 12 and certificates in production). API permissions → Microsoft Graph delegated permissions, including offline_access.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with your client ID and secret
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config for the outlook toolkit. Use the Entra application (client) ID, the client secret, and the same scopes you added in the registration.

steps.title: Set a custom publisher domain on the app
steps.detail: Verify a custom domain in the tenant by DNS. Set it as the app's publisher domain; *.onmicrosoft.com is not accepted. It must match the email domain on your Partner Program account.

steps.title: Add your PGA Partner One ID to request publisher verification
steps.time: Minutes once the prerequisites are met
steps.detail: Use the partner global account's Partner One ID (location IDs are rejected). Your partner email domain must match the publisher domain. You need Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator plus a Partner Center admin role, with MFA.

steps.title: Wait for Microsoft to process the verification
steps.time: Minutes if all requirements are met
steps.detail: After verification succeeds, the consent screen shows a blue badge and your publisher name instead of 'Unverified'. Recent developer reports describe portal failures; see blockers.

steps.title: Switch Composio connections to your own auth config
steps.detail: Point new connection requests at the custom auth config. Existing users connected through the managed app must reconnect to grant consent to your app.

steps.title: Get admin consent in each customer tenant
steps.detail: Send each customer's admin the admin-consent link. Required for mail and calendar scopes in tenants on the default policy, and for any tenant that blocks user consent.

values.label: Admin consent link (fill in your client ID)

steps.title: Test consent from an account in a different tenant
steps.detail: Confirm the consent screen shows your verified publisher name and that each capability works end to end.

steps.title: Optional: Microsoft 365 Certification
steps.detail: Not required to connect. A paid audit by Microsoft's assessor (Claranet): a 14-day document stage, then up to 60 days for evidence. Renewed every year. Some enterprise buyers ask for it.

gotchas.text: Microsoft's default consent policy now blocks user consent to mail, calendar, files and contacts-write permissions (rolled out July 2025 to July 2026). It applies to tenants on the Microsoft-managed policy; existing grants are unaffected.
Publisher verification does not exempt your app from those admin-consent requirements.
Access tokens last about an hour. Refresh tokens last 90 days and are replaced on each use; request offline_access to get one.
Client secrets expire after at most 24 months. Rotate them before they lapse or every connection breaks.
Outlook throttling is per app per mailbox: 10,000 requests per 10 minutes and 4 concurrent requests.
An app object cannot be moved between tenants. Register it in the tenant tied to your Partner Program account.
Publisher verification is not supported in national clouds or Azure AD B2C tenants.
The verified badge does not signal compliance or certification. Customers looking for that need Microsoft 365 Certification.

The API terms limit use of Outlook and Exchange mail APIs to syncing or backing up mail, calendar and contacts unless customers expressly grant other permissions. They also forbid creating copies of data beyond the intended usage and forbid using the data for advertising. Retained data must be deleted when a user leaves.

blockers.see: AADSTS50011: the redirect URI in the request does not match the redirect URIs configured for the application
blockers.cause: The redirect URI sent in the request differs from those registered on the Entra app.
blockers.fix: Register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add exactly on the app and confirm the Composio auth config uses the same app.

blockers.see: Publisher verification fails with 'MPN ID has not completed the vetting process' although Partner Center shows the account as verified
blockers.cause: Likely a partner location ID instead of the PGA ID, or a tenant not associated with the PGA.
blockers.fix: Use the partner global account Partner One ID and confirm the tenant is associated with the PGA. No confirmed fix was published; if it persists, raise it with Microsoft support.

blockers.see: Portal shows a 'temporary problem' when adding a Partner ID for publisher verification, lasting hours
blockers.fix: Retry later. The setVerifiedPublisher API is an alternative route, though it returned the vetting error in another report.

blockers.see: User from an associated tenant cannot complete publisher verification with a verified PartnerGlobal ID
blockers.cause: Verification requires the user to hold both the Entra role and the Partner Center role.
blockers.fix: Have a user with Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator plus Partner Admin or Account Admin, signed in with MFA, run the verification.

blockers.see: Cannot get publisher-verified status on an @onmicrosoft.com tenant
blockers.fix: Add and DNS-verify a custom domain matching your Partner Program email domain, then set it as the publisher domain.

aiPolicy.summary: Microsoft APIs Terms of Use have no AI-specific clause. General limits apply: minimum data and permissions, no copies or databases beyond the intended scenario, no resale or sublicensing of data, no advertising use, privacy statement as protective as Microsoft's, delete data when users leave. Outlook/Exchange data may only be used for sync or backup unless customers expressly grant other use.

customerAdminNote: In tenants on Microsoft's default consent policy, users can't grant mail, calendar or files access. Send their admin the admin-consent link from the steps.
